cards.explanation: The answer is dead, friends. Paul says it flat out: "And you were dead in your trespasses and sins…" (Ephesians 2:1). Not struggling, not limping along. Dead. That's why what comes next hits so hard.

The answer is False, friends. Paul describes "…the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience." (Ephesians 2:2). Now, as in still going. He doesn't say it packed up and left, so neither do I.

The answer is all of us, with Paul included, friends. Paul doesn't point a finger from a distance. He writes, "All of us also lived among them at one time…" (Ephesians 2:3). He puts himself right in the group. I like a teacher who says "us" and not "you people."
The answer is True, friends. Paul writes, "Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath." (Ephesians 2:3). Heavy line, I know. That's the "before," and Paul is about to flip the whole page.

The answer is that He loves us greatly, bakers. Paul says, "But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy…" (Ephesians 2:4). The reason is His love, plain and simple. We brought nothing to the table but crumbs, and He showed up anyway.

The answer is even when they were dead in their trespasses, friends. God's timing here is the worst possible time, and He shows up anyway. Paul says God "…made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses." (Ephesians 2:5). That's some kind of timing.
The answer is grace, bakers! Paul says, "It is by grace you have been saved!" (Ephesians 2:5). Look at that exclamation point on the end of the line. Grace is the word the verse lands on.

The answer is seated, bakers! Paul says God "…raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus…" (Ephesians 2:6). That comes right after Paul says God made us alive with Christ (Ephesians 2:5). So the picture goes from alive, to raised up, to seated, all with Christ.

The answer is to display the riches of His grace, friends. Paul says it was "…in order that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace…" (Ephesians 2:7). The purpose is to show off His grace. It's His kindness on display, not ours.

The answer is the gift of God, bakers! Paul says, "For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God…" (Ephesians 2:8). Not from ourselves, so it didn't start with us. It comes by grace through faith.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says salvation is "…not by works, so that no one can boast." (Ephesians 2:9). The reason is right there in the verse: no one can boast. Right before that, Paul says it's by grace through faith, and that it's the gift of God (Ephesians 2:8).

The answer is to do good works, friends! Paul says, "For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works…" (Ephesians 2:10). Good works are what we're created for, not how we get saved. Order matters here.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says the good works are ones "…which God prepared in advance as our way of life." (Ephesians 2:10). The text says God prepared them in advance. My own planning is mostly "more chocolate chips."
